title: Three Days in Toronto and a Danish Promise to Make Insulin
conflicts: Who prompted the Toronto visit: Krogh's own 1924 account does not mention Marie and says he heard of insulin on his US tour; Lindsten (Nobel essay) says Joslin told Marie at a dinner; the Novo Nordisk Foundation says Marie persuaded him. All three are given with attribution. Marie's diagnosis: 1920 (Dansk Kvindebiografisk Leksikon) vs probably 1921 (Lindsten); both given. Founding date: 1923 (Novo Nordisk Foundation, Lex.dk) vs Krogh's February 1924 agreement making it an independent non-profit institution; the story uses 1924 for independent non-profit status. Licence: 'licence' (Lindsten) vs 'exclusive right' (Lex.dk) vs Krogh's own 'delegated', with no legal protection; Krogh's wording used.
notes: Main source is Krogh's own 1924 Festschrift in the English translation published by the Novo Nordisk Foundation (memoir). The price comparison (about a tenth of the UK price) and the claim that no patient who had started went without are Krogh's own and attributed to him. The episode is set in Toronto and Copenhagen; country is Denmark. Lindsten spells Joslin 'Eliot'; the story uses Elliott.
